name: Ginger, Tulsi & Honey Infusion
desc: A widely used Indian kitchen remedy. Ginger (Shunthi/Ardraka) and Tulsi are traditionally used to ease throat irritation and congestion, and honey soothes the throat.
preparation: Boil the ginger and Tulsi leaves in water for 5-7 minutes.
Strain into a cup and let it cool until warm (not hot).
Stir in the honey only after it has cooled to drinking temperature.
usage: Sip warm, 2 times a day while symptoms last.
warning: Do not give honey to infants under 1 year. Ayurveda advises against heating honey. See a doctor if fever is high or symptoms last beyond 3 days.

name: Haldi Doodh (Turmeric Milk)
desc: Warm milk with turmeric and a pinch of black pepper is a traditional evening drink for a mild cough. Black pepper is commonly added alongside turmeric.
preparation: Warm the milk in a pan.
Add turmeric and black pepper and simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring.
Remove from heat, add jaggery if using, and drink warm.
usage: Once a day, preferably before bed.
warning: Avoid if you have a dairy allergy (use plant milk instead). People on blood thinners or with gallstones should check with a doctor before regular turmeric use. Seek care for cough with blood, breathlessness, or lasting more than 2 weeks.

name: Saunf & Mishri After Meals
desc: Chewing fennel seeds (saunf) with rock sugar (mishri) after meals is a common Indian practice. Fennel is considered cooling in Ayurveda and is used for mild acidity.
preparation: Mix fennel seeds and mishri.
Chew slowly after a meal.
usage: After lunch and dinner.
warning: People with diabetes should skip the mishri. Frequent or severe heartburn, difficulty swallowing, or chest pain needs a doctor's evaluation.

name: Cool Coriander Seed Water
desc: Coriander (Dhanyaka) is considered cooling and Pitta-pacifying in Ayurveda. Soaked coriander water is a traditional drink for a burning sensation from acidity.
preparation: Soak the crushed coriander seeds in water overnight.
Strain in the morning.
usage: Drink on an empty stomach in the morning.
warning: For mild symptoms only. Chest pain that spreads to the arm, jaw or back is an emergency, not acidity.

name: Ajwain & Black Salt Water
desc: Ajwain (carom seeds) is one of the most commonly used Indian kitchen remedies for gas and bloating after a heavy meal.
preparation: Lightly dry-roast the ajwain for a few seconds.
Add to warm water with the black salt, or chew the seeds and drink the warm water after.
usage: Once after a heavy meal, up to twice a day.
warning: Avoid large amounts during pregnancy. People on a low-salt diet for blood pressure should skip the black salt. Severe abdominal pain needs medical attention.

name: Hing (Asafoetida) in Warm Water
desc: A pinch of hing is used in Indian cooking to make lentils and beans easier to digest, and is also taken in warm water for gas.
preparation: Dissolve the hing in warm water and stir well.
usage: Once, after meals, when needed.
warning: Use only a pinch. Avoid during pregnancy and in young children unless advised by a doctor. Many commercial hing powders contain wheat flour, so check the label if you are gluten-intolerant.

name: Jeera (Cumin) Water
desc: Cumin is traditionally used in Ayurveda to support Agni (digestive fire). Jeera water is a simple everyday drink for a heavy stomach.
preparation: Boil cumin seeds in water for 5 minutes until the water turns light golden.
Strain and let it cool until warm.
usage: Sip warm after meals.
warning: For occasional indigestion only. Ongoing indigestion with weight loss, vomiting or black stools needs a doctor.

name: Spiced Takra (Buttermilk)
desc: Takra (thin buttermilk) is praised in classical Ayurvedic texts as an aid to digestion. It is traditionally taken with lunch, spiced with roasted cumin.
ingredients: Few fresh coriander or mint leaves
preparation: Whisk curd and water together until smooth.
Add the roasted cumin, salt and chopped leaves.
usage: One glass with or after lunch. Traditionally avoided at night.
warning: Avoid if you have a dairy allergy. Use fresh curd, not sour or stale.

name: Triphala Churna at Bedtime
desc: Triphala is a classical Ayurvedic blend of Amalaki, Bibhitaki and Haritaki, commonly used at bedtime as a gentle bowel regulator.
preparation: Mix the Triphala powder into warm water.
usage: Drink at bedtime. Start with the smaller dose.
warning: Not for pregnant or breastfeeding women, or children, without a doctor's advice. Stop if it causes diarrhoea or cramping. Constipation with blood or sudden change in bowel habits needs a doctor.

name: Warm Milk with Ghee
desc: A teaspoon of ghee in warm milk at night is a traditional remedy for dry, hard stools, which Ayurveda links to aggravated Vata.
preparation: Warm the milk and stir in the ghee.
usage: Drink at bedtime.
warning: Avoid with dairy allergy. People with high cholesterol or heart disease should ask their doctor before adding ghee regularly.

name: Warm Milk with a Pinch of Nutmeg
desc: Warm milk with a very small pinch of nutmeg (Jatiphala) is a traditional bedtime drink in Ayurveda for restlessness.
preparation: Warm the milk.
Add nutmeg and cardamom and stir well.
usage: 30 minutes before bed.
warning: Use only a tiny pinch. Nutmeg in larger amounts is toxic. Not for children or during pregnancy. Long-standing insomnia should be discussed with a doctor.

name: Fresh Ginger with Lemon
desc: Ginger is one of the best-known kitchen remedies for nausea, and is often chewed before travel.
ingredients: A thin slice of fresh ginger
A few drops of lemon juice
preparation: Sprinkle lemon juice and rock salt on the ginger slice.
usage: Chew slowly when nausea starts, or before a journey.
warning: Persistent vomiting, vomiting in pregnancy, or signs of dehydration need medical attention.

name: Warm Sesame Oil Massage (Abhyanga)
desc: Massage with warm sesame oil is a core Ayurvedic self-care practice, traditionally used for stiffness linked to Vata.
preparation: Warm the oil gently in a bowl placed in hot water.
Massage into the stiff joint in circular strokes for 10-15 minutes.
usage: Once a day, followed by a warm bath.
warning: Do not massage a joint that is red, hot or swollen, or after an injury. Test on a small patch first. Sudden severe joint pain needs a doctor.

name: Ajwain & Jaggery Tea
desc: A warm tea of ajwain with jaggery is a common household remedy for mild period cramps in many Indian homes.
preparation: Boil ajwain in water for 5 minutes.
Add jaggery, stir until dissolved, and strain.
usage: Sip warm, 1-2 times a day during cramps. A warm compress on the lower abdomen also helps.
warning: Very heavy bleeding, severe pain, or pain that is new for you should be checked by a gynaecologist.

name: Clove for Temporary Tooth Pain
desc: Clove (Lavanga) contains eugenol and has long been used in India and elsewhere for temporary toothache relief.
ingredients: 1 whole clove, or 1 drop clove oil diluted in 1/2 tsp coconut oil
preparation: Rinse the mouth with warm salt water.
Hold the clove against the painful tooth, or dab the diluted oil with a cotton swab.
usage: Up to 3 times a day until you can see a dentist.
warning: Temporary relief only. Never apply undiluted clove oil to gums. A toothache with facial swelling or fever needs a dentist urgently.

name: Coconut Oil for Dry, Itchy Skin
desc: Coconut oil is considered cooling in Ayurveda and is a traditional moisturiser for dry or mildly itchy skin.
preparation: Apply a thin layer to clean, slightly damp skin.
usage: 1-2 times a day, especially after a bath.
warning: Patch-test first. Do not use on broken skin, oozing rashes or infections. Hives with swelling of the lips or breathing trouble is an emergency.

name: Tulsi, Black Pepper & Ginger Kadha
desc: A kadha (decoction) of Tulsi, black pepper and ginger is one of the most common Indian home remedies taken during a mild cold with body ache.
preparation: Boil everything in water until it reduces to about 1 cup.
Strain and drink warm.
usage: Twice a day while symptoms last. Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
warning: Not a substitute for fever medicine or testing. See a doctor for fever above 102°F (38.9°C), fever lasting more than 3 days, rash, confusion, or any fever in an infant.

name: Amla (Indian Gooseberry)
desc: Amla is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C and is classed as a Rasayana (rejuvenative) in Ayurveda.
ingredients: 1 fresh amla, or 1 tsp amla powder
preparation: Eat the fresh amla with a pinch of salt, or mix amla powder in warm water with honey once it has cooled.
usage: Once daily in the morning.
warning: Ongoing tiredness can have medical causes such as anaemia or thyroid problems, so get a check-up if it lasts more than 2 weeks. People on diabetes or blood-thinning medicine should ask their doctor before regular use.

name: Cool Cucumber or Cold Compress
desc: Cool compresses over closed eyes are a simple, traditional way to relax tired eyes after long screen time.
ingredients: 2 slices chilled cucumber, or a clean cloth dipped in cool water
preparation: Lie back and place the cucumber slices or cool cloth over closed eyelids.
usage: 10 minutes, as needed. Also follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
warning: Do not put anything inside the eye. Eye pain, redness, discharge or changes in vision need an eye doctor.

name: Warm Coconut Oil Scalp Massage
desc: Oiling the scalp with coconut oil is a long-standing Indian hair-care practice for a dry scalp.
preparation: Warm the oil gently; you can heat the curry leaves in it until they crackle, then cool and strain.
Massage into the scalp with fingertips for 5-10 minutes.
usage: Leave on for an hour or overnight, then wash. 1-2 times a week.
warning: Sudden or patchy hair loss can signal thyroid, iron or other health issues, so see a doctor or dermatologist.

name: Temple Massage & Rest
desc: Gentle massage of the temples and forehead with a little oil, followed by rest in a quiet room, is a traditional way to ease a tension headache.
ingredients: A few drops of coconut or sesame oil
preparation: Drink a glass of water first, since dehydration is a common trigger.
Massage the temples and forehead in slow circles for 5 minutes, then rest with eyes closed.
usage: As needed.
warning: A sudden, severe 'worst-ever' headache, headache with fever and stiff neck, or with weakness or confusion, is an emergency.
